page: Amazon Web Services m8g.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Per-core cache architecture provides 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, supported by a 36 MB L3 cache. The instance operates without integrated local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes, while delivering 40 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight substantial parallel compute and memory throughput. In multi-threaded execution, the instance achieves top-tier results, reaching 163,469.47 in stress-ng multi-core and 26,119.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Software compilation via Clang (93,640.0) and ray tracing (106,623.0) both land in the top 10%. Memory subsystem bandwidth is exceptionally high, delivering 481.15 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 226.93 GB/sec for uncached writes, yielding a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,375.72. Networked application benchmarks confirm this throughput, demonstrated by 195.79 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 111.67 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

A key tradeoff stems from single-threaded core performance versus massive multi-core scaling. Single-core evaluations place m8g.24xlarge in the middle 50% across stress-ng (1,706.2) and Geekbench (1,882.0). Similarly, LLM inference text generation on lightweight 135M parameter models measures in the bottom 25% at 70.74 tokens/sec, whereas text generation on larger 7B and 70B models reaches top-tier throughput (50.93 tokens/sec and 7.08 tokens/sec, respectively) by leveraging the vast memory bandwidth and core density. The omission of local NVMe storage requires careful consideration for write-heavy persistent storage architectures.

The 96 dedicated ARM cores and high memory bandwidth deliver strong resource density and cost efficiency for horizontally scalable workloads. The instance is suited for high-concurrency web serving fleets, distributed database operations, large-scale CI/CD build farms, and memory-intensive caching systems like Redis.
